title: aws-well-architected-review structured output
description: Optional machine-readable companion to the aws-well-architected-review markdown report, written as aws-well-architected-review.json only when the user asks for JSON or structured output. The reviewing agent writes it from the self-checked BP ledger (the progress file and the per-shard ledger files) and the report, never invented; no validator ships with the skill, so a document is agent-checked against this schema, not machine-validated. It carries the same CONFIDENTIAL classification as the report. This schema is self-contained: it has no remote references and no runtime fetches.
x-attribution: Adapted from wa-review-v1.schema.json in aws-samples/sample-well-architected-skills-and-steering (pull request 119, commit 6e0c028), copyright Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates, licensed under MIT-0 (SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT-0). Structured-output design contributed by ajoshi01ai. Changes for this skill: numeric pillar scores removed in favor of per-pillar status counts; the five-value status vocabulary, per-BP read-proof ledger fields, corpus provenance, coverage audit, and remediation plan of this skill added.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the document conforms to. Any 1.x.y validates; a backward-compatible change bumps the minor or patch. Consumers reject on the major version only.

classification.description: Same classification as the markdown report. The document holds file paths, resource names, and unremediated gaps; handle it per references/security-considerations.md.

workload.description: Workload name exactly as it appears in the report title.

review_mode.description: Mode actually run. Only full and pillar-scoped reviews read BP pages; quick mode judges at question level and carries an empty ledger.

skill_version.description: The version value from the SKILL.md frontmatter that produced this document, as a string (for example "3").

run_id.description: The run identifier recorded in the run's progress file (corpus/progress.md) when the shards are planned. Distinguishes two reviews of the same workload on the same date.

business_criticality.description: Business criticality declared or established in Step 1.

lens.description: Names of the Well-Architected Lenses applied on top of the core framework. Omit or leave empty for a General review.

pillars.description: One entry per in-scope pillar with its status counts (replaces numeric pillar scores).

questions.description: Optional per-question assessment table from the report, one entry per assessed question.

ledger.description: One entry per in-scope BP that has a self-checked ledger row, taken from the progress file and the per-shard ledger files. Each entry is compact: status, risk, short evidence and the ledger file that holds the verbatim quotes and read proof. Empty for quick mode and for a user-accepted degraded run. Never contains a row that is not in the ledger.

findings.description: Risk-classified findings (Critical, High, Medium, Low) as reported, each citing the ledger BP IDs it expands.

status.description: The skill's five-value status vocabulary, spelled exactly as in references/evaluation-procedure.md and the report template.

bpId.description: Canonical framework best-practice ID as the skill writes it, for example SEC03-BP02. Copied verbatim from the corpus manifest; never invented.

lensBpId.description: Best-practice ID as published by a lens, which may use a longer prefix than the framework IDs.

questionId.description: Canonical question ID derived from the BP prefix, for example SEC03.

statusCounts.description: Count of BPs per status (questions per status in quick mode, where no BP pages are read). Keys are the exact status strings.

source.description: Index URL recorded in the manifest (the toc-contents.json URL on the normal path, the appendix or landing-page URL on the fallback path). Empty only for internal_knowledge_disclosed.

retrieved_at.description: UTC retrieval time of the index, ISO 8601.

pillar_id.description: pillar_id from the manifest (for example operational-excellence). Discovered live, so not an enum.

coverageAudit.description: Machine-readable form of the report's Coverage Audit. Counts are taken from the run's progress file, the same source as the report.

bps_in_scope.description: N as printed in the BP pages read line of the Coverage Audit: the manifest BP total for full and quick, the requested pillars' BP count for pillar-scoped.

bp_pages_read.description: Valid ledger rows that are not page_unreadable. Zero for quick mode and degraded runs.

fetch_tool_counts.description: Deprecated: kept only so that earlier 1.x documents still validate. This skill version never writes it; retrieval_method_counts is the single source for these counts.

retrieval_method_counts.description: Read rows per retrieval path: mcp_read (aws___read_documentation), web_fetch (HTTPS web-fetch tool, only after a real aws___read_documentation error for that page, or for every page when the session had no such tool).

gate.description: Deprecated: kept only so that earlier 1.x documents still validate. This skill version never writes it, because nothing in its procedure records these counts.

invalid.description: A document is only written after every serialized row passed its self-check.

spot_check.description: The fixed-size spot-check: pages re-read by the agent to confirm the rows' quotes. Null for quick mode and degraded runs, which have no spot-check.

mode_note.description: Required wording for quick mode, a degraded run, or a partial run (complete false), copied from the report's BP pages read or Review status line.

complete.description: False when the run ended before every in-scope shard was self-checked and spot-checked (a partial report). Absent means true.

pending_bp_ids.description: In-scope BPs with no accepted ledger row yet (partial run only). bps_in_scope equals the ledger entries plus these.

read_proof.description: Added in 1.3.0. The read proof and the spot-check were checked by the reviewing agent, not machine-verified.

evidence_ledger.description: Added in 1.3.0. Absolute path of the evidence ledger folder (aws-well-architected-review-ledger/) whose per-shard files hold the verbatim quotes and read proof of every row.

errorCode.description: The documentation tool's enumerated error codes.

file.description: Path of the evidence within the declared workload scope.

note.description: Tool evidence or free text (for example Based on description). Secrets MUST be redacted: identify the secret type and location, never the value.

ledgerEntry.description: One self-checked ledger row in compact form (changed in 1.3.0: only the fields above are required; ledger_file, added in 1.3.0, stays optional so that any 1.x document validates). Field names and meanings match the Row fields table in references/evaluation-procedure.md, except that its url field is bp_url here and its read line (total_length, end_index, truncated) is split into the three fields of those names. The verbatim quotes and read proof stay in the per-shard ledger file named in ledger_file; a writer may copy them here, in which case the optional fields below apply. The equality end_index == total_length cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and is part of the agent's row self-check.

bp_url.description: The manifest BP URL, verbatim. On the fallback path (manifest href empty) the docs.aws.amazon.com URL the reader located; empty only when the URL could not be located (page_unreadable).

ledger_file.description: Added in 1.3.0 (optional in the schema so that earlier 1.x documents validate; this skill version always writes it). The shard file in the evidence ledger folder that holds this row's verbatim quotes and read proof, for example S07.md.

fetch_tool.description: Deprecated: kept only so that earlier 1.x documents still validate. This skill version never writes it; retrieval_method is the single source for the read path.

retrieval_method.description: How this BP page was read: mcp_read (aws___read_documentation) or web_fetch (HTTPS web-fetch tool, after a real aws___read_documentation error or when the session had no such tool). Required on every row that is not page_unreadable.

mcp_error.description: Raw aws___read_documentation error, or aws___read_documentation not available in this session when the session had no such tool; required and non-empty when retrieval_method is web_fetch.

source_chars.description: Optional; kept for compatibility with 1.0 and 1.1 documents.

outcome_quote.description: Optional copy of the row's verbatim passage from the Desired outcome paragraph (or the page opening), 80-300 characters; empty only for page_unreadable rows.

tail_quote.description: Optional copy of the row's verbatim passage from the end of the page body, 80-300 characters; empty only for page_unreadable rows.

antipattern_hit.description: Verbatim anti-pattern the workload evidence matches, or the string none.

evidence.description: Short evidence: usually one item with its provenance tag and file/line or a short note.

reason.description: Optional: one sentence tying the status to the quoted outcome or anti-pattern and the evidence, or the exact string page_unreadable (required for an unreadable row).

risk_level.description: Null for Implemented, Not Applicable, and Cannot Determine.

recommendation.description: Optional concrete next step for a gap row; prose guidance, never a code diff.

allOf.$comment: A gap must be rated: a consumer ranking by risk would otherwise fail open.
A satisfied, inapplicable, or undeterminable BP carries no risk: a consumer ranking by risk would otherwise see a phantom risk.
An unreadable page carries its tool error and zero counts; every other row names how its page was read and, when read-proof fields are copied, carries full-read values.

finding.description: A reported finding. A framework finding cites the ledger BP IDs it expands in bp_ids. A finding from a topic-organized lens that publishes no BP IDs carries lens instead and omits bp_ids; a review-integrity finding that no reviewed BP fits carries review_integrity instead and omits bp_ids; never invent an ID.

review_integrity.description: Marks a review-integrity finding: instruction-like text in the workload content, reported as a possible prompt-injection attempt (references/security-considerations.md). It cites its file and line in evidence; bp_ids is optional on it. Added in 1.4.0.

bp_text_cited.description: Outcome or anti-pattern quoted from the BP page via the ledger row.

remediationPlan.description: The report's Prioritized Remediation Plan. Quick Wins (under 1 week, Do First), Foundation (1-4 weeks, Plan), Strategic (1-3 months, Plan), then Delegate and Deferred. Arrays may be empty.
